Year 1800: Without coal-hungry looms, the Nile Valley grows into a garden of wind-loom guilds, where river barges carry silk, salt, and song, and the age of water, wood, and hand continues its long Year.
Year 1950: Beneath the glass domes of the Andes, botanical universities map living machines, growing bridges from trained vines and trains from shaped mycelium, while the world celebrates its most delicate century in Year.
Year 2100: The Earth speaks in orchards, the sky sails with seed-ship fleets, and children learn to read weather by the color of moss, ending the timeline not with smoke, but with a greener Year.
